# Career Brief: Breaking into Post-Production IT/Engineering in LA

## 1) What M&E employers actually expect (recurring requirements)
Synthesized from three real sources I read: a post-production engineer job description (jobed.ai), Amazon MGM Studios' live Production Workflow Engineer posting, and Paramount's live Senior Manager, Media Operations posting.

**Three requirements that recur across all of them:**
1. **Fluency in professional post tools + codecs/formats** — Avid Media Composer, Avid NEXIS, Blackmagic DaVinci Resolve, Adobe (Premiere/CC); working knowledge of media formats, codecs, and editorial workflows (dailies, conform, color, mastering).
2. **Media infrastructure ownership** — shared/networked storage, backup and archive strategy, media asset management (MAM/DAM), enterprise file transfer (Signiant/Media Shuttle, Aspera), and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, OCI).
3. **Core IT systems skills in a production context** — hardware/software troubleshooting, server/workstation administration (Windows/macOS/Linux), security and access provisioning (e.g., Active Directory), and vendor/tool management — all in service of editorial continuity.

Secondary recurring items: a bachelor's in media technology/engineering (often waivable with equivalent experience), and experience supporting editors/creatives under tight deadlines.

## 2) Two concrete training/certification routes
**Route A — Avid track (the industry-standard post credential path).** California's registered apprenticeship standard for "Media & Entertainment Post Production Engineer" (apprenticeshipstandards.org, standard 27-4032.00) graduates with industry certifications including **Avid User Certified, Assistant Editor Certified, Avid Engineering Certified, and Avid Shared Storage Certified**. Its on-the-job training outline is essentially a post-IT syllabus: maintain/operate servers, storage servers and workstations on Windows/macOS/Linux; set up and maintain shared storage and networked systems; manage virtual machines; troubleshoot and document systems; run QC (verify timecodes/file locations); set up remote/offsite post systems. Pairing Avid Engineering + Avid Shared Storage certs with any storage/IT background maps directly to the recurring requirements above.

**Route B — Cloud + enterprise media-transfer track.** The two live postings both demand cloud engineering: Amazon requires **AWS services (EC2, S3, Route53, VPC)** and content-security standards; Paramount requires **AWS/Azure/OCI cloud storage plus Signiant/Media Shuttle and Aspera**. A realistic route: **AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner → AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate**, plus hands-on with enterprise file transfer (Signiant/Aspera) and, for the IT floor, CompTIA A+/Network+. This is the path for the "IT engineer supporting post" lane rather than the creative-workflow lane.

Both routes are trainable in months-to-a-year or two with focused study; neither requires a union card to start.

## 3) Local 700 (Motion Picture Editors Guild) — West Coast entry path
Note: iatse700.org was unreachable (connection reset); the guild's real site is **editorsguild.com**. Key pages I opened: Join West Coast (the exact wording, left open) and the Organizing FAQ.

**The actual sequence (from editorsguild.com/Join/Join-West-Coast):**
1. **Get a union job first.** The Guild "encourages prospective members to first secure a union job." Once union employment begins, you **must join Local 700 within 30 days of your date of hire**.
2. **Get on the CSATF Industry Experience Roster (usually before you're hired).** Most classifications working in **Los Angeles County** must be on the **CSATF Industry Experience Roster** *prior to accepting union employment* — employers must give preference of employment to rostered people. Exceptions: Foley Artist and Sound Service Person (Y16); some employers don't require it (verify with Membership staff). **Roster placement and union membership are separate processes** — one does not trigger the other.
3. **Roster eligibility & paperwork.** Experience must be the kind covered by Local 700 agreements or the Videotape Supplemental Agreement, performed in the US and/or Puerto Rico. Documentaries must have screened (festival/TV/theater); **industrial/educational films do NOT count**; SVOD eligibility varies. You must submit **BOTH** (a) a letter from the non-union employer on company letterhead (or from the payroll company if paid through one) **AND** (b) proof of payment — W-2s, 1099s, paystubs, or cancelled checks — at no less than California minimum wage.
4. **Roster application: $0 fee**, handled online through the CSATF portal (**thehub.org**).
5. **Safety courses (required for all classifications):** **A – General Production Safety, HP1, and WVP** (Sound classifications also take Course K).
6. **Required experience days vary by classification** — the page has a per-classification selector (Editor, Engineer, Technical Director, VFX Editor, etc.); the exact day counts are on that page, and a CSATF Roster Specialist can verify whether your specific experience qualifies.
7. **New Member Orientation** via Zoom (covers roster application, membership responsibilities, pension/health benefits, organizers/field reps) — schedule through the page.
8. **Initiation & processing fee:** one-time, varies by the contract your employer/project is signed to. Payment plan available: **half down, half within 6 months**; checks, money orders, credit cards accepted. (The "View Initiation Fees" link didn't expose fixed dollar amounts to me — call Membership for the current figure.)
9. **Contacts:** Membership Dept. — Tracy Pacio (323) 978-1087, Tylene Joye (323) 978-1085, membership@editorsguild.com. CSATF — 2710 Winona Ave, Burbank, CA 91504, (818) 565-0550, reception@csatf.org.

**Realistic read:** the union route is *experience-gated, not training-gated* — you need documented, qualifying non-union days in the craft (with employer letters + pay proof) to get rostered, then a union hire to trigger membership. For IT/engineering support roles, the practical sequence is: get non-union post-IT experience (even at a small post house or via the apprenticeship route) → get rostered in the relevant classification (e.g., Engineer/Technical Director) → take a union job → join within 30 days.

## 4) Current LA/West Coast postings that match (both opened in tabs)
**Job 1 — Amazon MGM Studios: Production Workflow Engineer, Production Technology Engineering (Job ID 10485237)** — **Culver City, CA** (Amazon Studios LLC). Drives adoption of cloud post workflows (dailies, editorial, conform, color, mastering, remote production). Requires: Avid Media Composer, Avid NEXIS, Blackmagic Resolve, Colorfront On-Set Dailies/Transkoder, Adobe CC; AWS (EC2, S3, Route53, VPC); 2+ yrs design/implementation/consulting + 4+ yrs in a tech domain; post-workflow M&E experience. **Salary: $131,300–$177,600 base** + sign-on/RSUs. **Visa/work authorization: not mentioned** in the posting (standard EOE language only). *Connection: hits all three recurring requirements — post tools/codecs, cloud + media workflows, systems engineering.*

**Job 2 — Paramount (Paramount Skydance): Senior Manager, Media Operations** — **Los Angeles (Hollywood), CA** (1575 Gower), posted **Sept 2, 2026**. Owns storage/archive strategy (on-prem + cloud), access provisioning and auditing, AD security groups, live/near-live ingest (WildMoka, movie recorder routing), enterprise file transfer (Signiant/Media Shuttle, Aspera), MAM/DAM, vendor management. Requires 5 yrs in media management, post-production operations, or media infrastructure/IT; Avid/Premiere/Resolve; AWS/Azure/OCI. **Salary: $98,000–$125,000.** **Visa/work authorization: not mentioned** in the posting. *Connection: the purest "IT for post" posting of the two — storage, security/access, file transfer, MAM — though it's a senior/managerial level, useful as a 3–5 year target rather than an entry point.*

Honest caveat: neither posting advertises visa sponsorship; Amazon's posting also notes LA County Fair Chance Ordinance language. Entry-level versions of these roles (post-production IT support, post engineer I, media coordinator) are where the realistic first step is — the EntertainmentCareers.net board (entertainmentcareers.net, Santa Monica-based) is where these get posted.

## 5) Rosie O'Donnell / Trump feud — dated timeline (from Business Insider & CNN timelines)
- **Dec 19, 2006** — Trump holds a press conference on Miss USA Tara Conner (drug allegations) and decides *not* to strip her crown, offering a "second chance" and rehab.
- **Dec 20, 2006** — O'Donnell, then co-host of *The View*, criticizes the decision, calling Trump a "snake-oil salesman on Little House on the Prairie" and citing his bankruptcies and marriages. Trump fires back in *People* magazine, calling her "a real loser" and "a woman out of control," threatening to sue.
- **May 2007** — O'Donnell leaves *The View* after a Hasselbeck spat; Trump tells *Extra* "I think Rosie should win, but Rosie is not much herself."
- **Dec 14, 2011** — After O'Donnell announces her engagement to Michelle Rounds, Trump tweets he feels "sorry" for Rounds' parents, calling Rosie "a true loser"; O'Donnell replies "u r an ass in every way."
- **Aug 21, 2012** — After O'Donnell's heart attack, Trump tweets "Rosie, get better fast. I'm starting to miss you!" — a brief thaw.
- **May 11, 2017** — Trump resurrects her Dec 20, 2016 "FIRE COMEY" tweet: "Rosie, we finally agree on something."
- **Jan 2025** (per US Magazine/worldwire summaries in search results) — After O'Donnell's move to Ireland, Trump warns he could revoke her U.S. citizenship, reigniting the feud.

## 6) Bottom line
- **Realistic entry path:** non-union post-IT experience first (post house, VFX vendor, or the CA apprenticeship route) → build the Avid + storage/cloud credential stack → target "post-production IT support / post engineer" roles → get CSATF rostered once you have documented qualifying days → take a union job and join Local 700 within 30 days.
- **Is it trainable?** Yes for the skills (both cert routes are concrete and public); the union step itself is gated on documented industry experience, not coursework.

## Tabs left open for you
1. **editorsguild.com/Join/Join-West-Coast** ← **the most useful Local 700 page — read this for the exact West Coast wording** (roster rules, 30-day rule, fees, contacts)
2. editorsguild.com Organizing FAQ (second Local 700 page — organizing/dues/contract questions)
3. Business Insider — full dated feud timeline
4. Amazon MGM Studios — Production Workflow Engineer posting (Culver City)
5. Paramount — Senior Manager, Media Operations posting (LA/Hollywood)
6. apprenticeshipstandards.org — Media & Entertainment Post Production Engineer apprenticeship standard (training route A)

Caveats: I couldn't extract Local 700's exact per-classification roster day counts (they're behind a client-side dropdown on the Join West Coast page) or the exact initiation-fee dollar amounts (the fees link redirected to the general Join page) — call the Membership Dept. at (323) 978-1087 for both. Google search was captcha-blocked throughout, so I used DuckDuckGo and direct site navigation.

Its on-the-job training outline is essentially a post-IT syllabus: maintain/operate servers, storage servers and workstations on Windows/macOS/Linux; set up and maintain shared storage and networked systems; manage virtual machines; troubleshoot and document systems; run QC (verify timecodes/file locations); set up remote/offsite post systems. Pairing Avid Engineering + Avid Shared Storage certs with any storage/IT background maps directly to the recurring requirements above.

**Route B — Cloud + enterprise media-transfer track.** The two live postings both demand cloud engineering: Amazon requires **AWS services (EC2, S3, Route53, VPC)** and content-security standards; Paramount requires **AWS/Azure/OCI cloud storage plus Signiant/Media Shuttle and Aspera**. A realistic route: **AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner → AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate**, plus hands-on with enterprise file transfer (Signiant/Aspera) and, for the IT floor, CompTIA A+/Network+. This is the path for the "IT engineer supporting post" lane rather than the creative-workflow lane.

Both routes are trainable in months-to-a-year or two with focused study; neither requires a union card to start.

## 3) Local 700 (Motion Picture Editors Guild) — West Coast entry path
Note: iatse700.org was unreachable (connection reset); the guild's real site is **editorsguild.com**. Key pages I opened: Join West Coast (the exact wording, left open) and the Organizing FAQ.

**The actual sequence (from editorsguild.com/Join/Join-West-Coast):**
1. **Get a union job first.** The Guild "encourages prospective members to first secure a union job." Once union employment begins, you **must join Local 700 within 30 days of your date of hire**.
2. **Get on the CSATF Industry Experience Roster (usually before you're hired).** Most classifications working in **Los Angeles County** must be on the **CSATF Industry Experience Roster** *prior to accepting union employment* — employers must give preference of employment to rostered people. Exceptions: Foley Artist and Sound Service Person (Y16); some employers don't require it (verify with Membership staff). **Roster placement and union membership are separate processes** — one does not trigger the other.
3. **Roster eligibility & paperwork.** Experience must be the kind covered by Local 700 agreements or the Videotape Supplemental Agreement, performed in the US and/or Puerto Rico. Documentaries must have screened (festival/TV/theater); **industrial/educational films do NOT count**; SVOD eligibility varies. You must submit **BOTH** (a) a letter from the non-union employer on company letterhead (or from the payroll company if paid through one) **AND** (b) proof of payment — W-2s, 1099s, paystubs, or cancelled checks — at no less than California minimum wage.
4. **Roster application: $0 fee**, handled online through the CSATF portal (**thehub.org**).
5. **Safety courses (required for all classifications):** **A – General Production Safety, HP1, and WVP** (Sound classifications also take Course K).
6. **Required experience days vary by classification** — the page has a per-classification selector (Editor, Engineer, Technical Director, VFX Editor, etc.); the exact day counts are on that page, and a CSATF Roster Specialist can verify whether your specific experience qualifies.
7. **New Member Orientation** via Zoom (covers roster application, membership responsibilities, pension/health benefits, organizers/field reps) — schedule through the page.
8. **Initiation & processing fee:** one-time, varies by the contract your employer/project is signed to. Payment plan available: **half down, half within 6 months**; checks, money orders, credit cards accepted. (The "View Initiation Fees" link didn't expose fixed dollar amounts to me — call Membership for the current figure.)
9. **Contacts:** Membership Dept. — Tracy Pacio (323) 978-1087, Tylene Joye (323) 978-1085, membership@editorsguild.com. CSATF — 2710 Winona Ave, Burbank, CA 91504, (818) 565-0550, reception@csatf.org.

**Realistic read:** the union route is *experience-gated, not training-gated* — you need documented, qualifying non-union days in the craft (with employer letters + pay proof) to get rostered, then a union hire to trigger membership. For IT/engineering support roles, the practical sequence is: get non-union post-IT experience (even at a small post house or via the apprenticeship route) → get rostered in the relevant classification (e.g., Engineer/Technical Director) → take a union job → join within 30 days.

## 4) Current LA/West Coast postings that match (both opened in tabs)
**Job 1 — Amazon MGM Studios: Production Workflow Engineer, Production Technology Engineering (Job ID 10485237)** — **Culver City, CA** (Amazon Studios LLC). Drives adoption of cloud post workflows (dailies, editorial, conform, color, mastering, remote production). Requires: Avid Media Composer, Avid NEXIS, Blackmagic Resolve, Colorfront On-Set Dailies/Transkoder, Adobe CC; AWS (EC2, S3, Route53, VPC); 2+ yrs design/implementation/consulting + 4+ yrs in a tech domain; post-workflow M&E experience. **Salary: $131,300–$177,600 base** + sign-on/RSUs. **Visa/work authorization: not mentioned** in the posting (standard EOE language only). *Connection: hits all three recurring requirements — post tools/codecs, cloud + media workflows, systems engineering.*

**Job 2 — Paramount (Paramount Skydance): Senior Manager, Media Operations** — **Los Angeles (Hollywood), CA** (1575 Gower), posted **Sept 2, 2026**. Owns storage/archive strategy (on-prem + cloud), access provisioning and auditing, AD security groups, live/near-live ingest (WildMoka, movie recorder routing), enterprise file transfer (Signiant/Media Shuttle, Aspera), MAM/DAM, vendor management. Requires 5 yrs in media management, post-production operations, or media infrastructure/IT; Avid/Premiere/Resolve; AWS/Azure/OCI. **Salary: $98,000–$125,000.** **Visa/work authorization: not mentioned** in the posting. *Connection: the purest "IT for post" posting of the two — storage, security/access, file transfer, MAM — though it's a senior/managerial level, useful as a 3–5 year target rather than an entry point.*

Honest caveat: neither posting advertises visa sponsorship; Amazon's posting also notes LA County Fair Chance Ordinance language. Entry-level versions of these roles (post-production IT support, post engineer I, media coordinator) are where the realistic first step is — the EntertainmentCareers.net board (entertainmentcareers.net, Santa Monica-based) is where these get posted.
